exercises.task:
1. Crea un PVC chiamato 'data-pvc'
2. Richiedi 1Gi di storage
3. Usa la StorageClass predefinita
4. Specifica modalità di accesso ReadWriteOnce
hints: kubectl create è limitato per PVC, usa manifest YAML
spec.accessModes per la modalità di accesso
exercises.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: data-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
EOF

title.it: Usare un PVC in un pod
title.en: Use a PVC in a pod

description.it: Montare un volume persistente in un container
description.en: Mount a persistent volume in a container

exercises.task:
1. Crea un pod che monta il PVC 'data-pvc'
2. Monta il volume su /data
3. Verifica che il volume sia montato correttamente
4. Scrivi un file di test
hints: kubectl exec per scrivere il file
exercises.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: storage-pod
spec:
  volumes:
  - name: data
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: data-pvc
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx
    volumeMounts:
    - name: data
      mountPath: /data
EOF

kubectl exec storage-pod -- touch /data/test.txt
kubectl exec storage-pod -- ls /data/

exercises.task:
1. Crea un PV 'local-pv' con capacity 5Gi
2. Usa accessMode ReadWriteOnce
3. Imposta hostPath su /mnt/data
4. Crea un PVC che lo binda
exercises.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: local-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 5Gi
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce

    path: /mnt/data
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: local-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
EOF

description.it: Definire una classe di storage per provisioning dinamico
description.en: Define a storage class for dynamic provisioning

exercises.task:
1. Crea una StorageClass 'fast-storage'
2. Usa provisioner kubernetes.io/no-provisioner (simula)
3. Imposta reclaim policy Delete
4. Crea un PVC che la usa
exercises.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: fast-storage
provisioner: kubernetes.io/no-provisioner
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
EOF

cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: fast-pvc
spec:
  storageClassName: fast-storage
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 2Gi
EOF

exercises.task:
1. Crea un pod con due container
2. Condividi un emptyDir tra i container
3. Il primo container scrive un file
4. Il secondo container legge il file
hints: emptyDir è cancellato al pod restart
I container devono montare lo stesso volume
Usa command per automatizzare la scrittura
exercises.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: shared-pod
spec:
  volumes:
  - name: shared
    emptyDir: {}
  containers:
  - name: writer
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'echo "Hello from writer" > /data/message.txt && sleep 3600']
    volumeMounts:
    - name: shared
      mountPath: /data
  - name: reader
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'sleep 5 && cat /data/message.txt && sleep 3600']
    volumeMounts:
    - name: shared
      mountPath: /data
EOF

kubectl logs shared-pod -c reader

description.it: Creare deployment con storage persistente per replica
description.en: Create deployment with persistent storage per replica

exercises.task:
1. Crea uno StatefulSet 'web-db' con 2 repliche
2. Usa volumeClaimTemplate per 1Gi storage per replica
3. Verifica che ogni replica abbia il suo PVC
4. Controlla i nomi dei PVC
exercises.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: web-db
spec:
  serviceName: web-db
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web-db
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web-db
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: data
    spec:
      accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 1Gi
EOF

kubectl get pvc | grep data-web-db
exercises.validation: kubectl get pvc -l app=web-db -o name | wc -l

exercises.task:
1. Crea un pod con un PVC montato
2. Aggiungi un init container che crea una directory e scarica dati
3. Il container principale legge i dati preparati
4. Verifica che i dati siano presenti
hints: Init containers girano prima dei container principali
Entrambi devono montare lo stesso volume
Usa wget o curl per scaricare dati
exercises.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: init-demo
spec:
  volumes:
  - name: workdir
    emptyDir: {}
  initContainers:
  - name: setup
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'mkdir -p /data && echo "Initialized at $(date)" > /data/status.txt']
    volumeMounts:
    - name: workdir
      mountPath: /data
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'cat /data/status.txt && sleep 3600']
    volumeMounts:
    - name: workdir
      mountPath: /data
EOF

kubectl logs init-demo | grep Initialized

description.it: Creare storage condiviso tra più pod
description.en: Create storage shared between multiple pods

exercises.task:
1. Crea una StorageClass con provisioner NFS (simulato)
2. Crea un PVC con accessMode ReadWriteMany
3. Crea due pod che montano lo stesso PVC
4. Verifica che il file scritto da uno sia leggibile dall'altro
hints: RWX richiede storage backend che lo supporta (NFS)
Lo stesso PVC può essere montato da più pod
In assenza di NFS, usa hostPath per test locali
exercises.solution:
# Nota: RWX richiede NFS o simile. Demo con shared hostPath:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: shared-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 1Gi
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteMany
  hostPath:
    path: /tmp/shared-data
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: shared-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
EOF

cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: writer
spec:
  volumes:
  - name: shared
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: shared-pvc
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'echo "shared data" > /data/file.txt && sleep 3600']
    volumeMounts:
    - name: shared
      mountPath: /data
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: reader
spec:
  volumes:
  - name: shared
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: shared-pvc
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'sleep 5 && cat /data/file.txt && sleep 3600']
    volumeMounts:
    - name: shared
      mountPath: /data
EOF

description.it: Usare un Secret come file nel pod
description.en: Use a Secret as file in the pod

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Secret 'db-credentials' con username e password
2. Monta il Secret come volume su /etc/secrets
3. Verifica che i file siano creati correttamente
4. Leggi il contenuto dei file
hints: Ogni chiave del Secret diventa un file
exercises.solution:
kubectl create secret generic db-credentials --from-literal=username=admin --from-literal=password=secret123

cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secret-pod
spec:
  volumes:
  - name: secrets
    secret:
      secretName: db-credentials
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'ls -la /etc/secrets && cat /etc/secrets/username && sleep 3600']
    volumeMounts:
    - name: secrets
      mountPath: /etc/secrets
EOF

kubectl exec secret-pod -- cat /etc/secrets/password
exercises.validation: kubectl exec secret-pod -- ls /etc/secrets | grep username

description.it: Usare una ConfigMap come file di configurazione
description.en: Use a ConfigMap as configuration file

exercises.task:
1. Crea una ConfigMap 'app-config' con un file nginx.conf
2. Monta la ConfigMap su /etc/nginx/conf.d
3. Verifica che la configurazione sia applicata
4. Aggiorna la ConfigMap e osserva il cambiamento
hints: Le ConfigMap possono essere montate come file
exercises.solution:
kubectl create configmap app-config --from-literal=config.js='export default { api: "http://api.example.com" };'

cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: config-pod
spec:
  volumes:
  - name: config
    configMap:
      name: app-config
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'cat /etc/config/config.js && sleep 3600']
    volumeMounts:
    - name: config
      mountPath: /etc/config
EOF

description.it: Accedere al volume come block device

exercises.task:
1. Crea un PV con volumeMode: Block
2. Crea un PVC che lo usa
3. Monta il volume in un pod come block device
4. Verifica con lsblk o fdisk
hints: Il pod deve avere permessi per accedere al device
exercises.solution:
# Nota: Block mode richiede CSI driver che lo supporta
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: block-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 1Gi
  volumeMode: Block
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  hostPath:
    path: /tmp/block-dev
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: block-pvc
spec:
  volumeMode: Block
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
EOF

description.it: Aumentare la dimensione di un PVC esistente
description.en: Increase size of an existing PVC

exercises.task:
1. Crea una StorageClass con allowVolumeExpansion: true
2. Crea un PVC da 1Gi
3. Espandi il PVC a 2Gi con kubectl patch
4. Verifica la nuova dimensione
hints: kubectl patch pvc per aggiornare la dimensione
Alcuni CSI non supportano la riduzione
exercises.solution:
# Verifica se la StorageClass di default supporta espansione
kubectl get storageclass -o yaml | grep -A2 allowVolumeExpansion

# Se supportata, espandi il PVC
kubectl patch pvc data-pvc -p '{"spec": {"resources": {"requests": {"storage": "2Gi"}}}}'

kubectl get pvc data-pvc

description.it: Selezionare PV specifico con label selector
description.en: Select specific PV with label selector

exercises.task:
1. Crea un PV con label 'tier: database'
2. Crea un PVC con selector che matcha il label
3. Verifica che il PVC si binda al PV corretto
4. Crea un pod che lo usa
hints: Il binding è automatico se il selector matcha
exercises.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: db-pv
  labels:
    tier: database
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 10Gi
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  hostPath:
    path: /mnt/db-data
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: db-pvc
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      tier: database
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 10Gi
EOF

description.it: Creare uno snapshot di un volume

exercises.task:
1. Crea un VolumeSnapshotClass
2. Crea un VolumeSnapshot del PVC
3. Verifica lo stato dello snapshot
4. Crea un nuovo PVC dallo snapshot
hints: Richiede CSI driver con supporto snapshot
exercises.solution:
# Nota: Richiede CSI con supporto snapshot
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: snapshot.storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: VolumeSnapshotClass
metadata:
  name: default-snapclass
driver: hostpath.csi.k8s.io
deletionPolicy: Delete
---
apiVersion: snapshot.storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: VolumeSnapshot
metadata:
  name: data-snapshot
spec:
  volumeSnapshotClassName: default-snapclass
  source:
    persistentVolumeClaimName: data-pvc
EOF

# Restaurare dallo snapshot
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: restored-pvc
spec:
  dataSource:
    name: data-snapshot
    kind: VolumeSnapshot
    apiGroup: snapshot.storage.k8s.io
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
EOF

description.it: Deployare un database con storage persistente e backup
description.en: Deploy a database with persistent storage and backup

exercises.task:
1. Crea uno StatefulSet PostgreSQL con 1 replica
2. Usa volumeClaimTemplate per i dati
3. Configura init container per setup DB
4. Crea un Job di backup che usa lo stesso storage
hints: StatefulSet con serviceName per DNS stabile
Init container per creare database iniziale
Job con lo stesso PVC per backup
exercises.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: postgres
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: postgres
  ports:
  - port: 5432
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: postgres
spec:
  serviceName: postgres
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: postgres
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: postgres
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: postgres
        image: postgres:15
        env:
        - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
          value: postgres
        ports:
        - containerPort: 5432
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: data
    spec:
      accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 5Gi
EOF
